summary: Session 2: the extension's module lifecycle is now thin launchers over `python -m ai_router.modules`, and the command is visible. All five context-menu commands (ids unchanged) run the CLI through the resolved workspace-venv interpreter, echo the exact copy-pasteable command line to a shared 'Dabbler Commands' output channel before spawning, and branch on the published exit codes (3 = refused, nothing written; 4 = write failure, with rolledBack distinguishing 'unchanged' from 'reconcile from git'). The TypeScript lifecycle they replaced is deleted, not left beside them: moduleAuthoring.ts 2601 -> 608 lines. Per operator decision the TypeScript session-state.json writer went too -- ai_router.session_lifecycle gained a cancel/restore CLI, cancelLifecycleCommands.ts routes through it, and cancelLifecycle.ts 549 -> 142 lines of readers -- so the invariant this whole set exists to restore is actually restored. Also: gitScaffold's default-module scaffold is Python-backed, copyModuleDecompositionPrompt is on the module context menu, residual S122-S1-R1 is closed, and start_session now ticks its own `register` step (operator-directed).

reason.specifics: Run SESSION 4 NEXT, not Session 3 (operator decision, 2026-08-13, journalled). Session 2 made the extension depend on `python -m ai_router.modules`, and Session 4 owns the guarantee that the module is there and new enough -- the version floor, the upgrade-capable install, the capability probe and the retryability fix. It is also the release gate for both registries. Two carry-ins make it same-surface continuation rather than fresh-eyes work: residual S122-S2-R3 (nothing now asserts the PUBLISHED wheel is compatible; that check moved to the release walk and needs building there), and the `DABBLER_ROUTER_INSTALL_SPEC` seam this session added, which is exactly where a registry-versus-local install assertion belongs. Session 3 (append-file partitioning) is independent of both and can follow.

residuals.source: Full Layer 3 run of record (npm run test:playwright), 2026-08-13
residuals.description: `vsix-first-run-walkthrough.spec.ts` went RED when the default-module scaffold became Python-backed. It performs a real `pip install` from a genuinely empty folder, but it resolved `dabbler-ai-router` from live PyPI -- 0.34.0, a wheel released before `ai_router.modules` existed -- so the scaffold could not run and the tree stalled at `Default0 sets`.
residuals.rationale: Diagnosed as structural rather than incidental: a test that installs from the registry can only ever validate the LAST PUBLISHED wheel against the CURRENT extension, so once the extension depended on unreleased router code the walk was red until a publish it is itself supposed to gate -- Session 4 could not have fixed it either. Operator decision 2026-08-13 (journalled): split the two questions. `DABBLER_ROUTER_INSTALL_SPEC` (harness-only, the `DABBLER_STARTUP_TIMING_PATH` precedent) points the walk at this repo, so it still starts from an empty folder with a real git init, a real venv and a real pip install -- L-079-3 intact -- and now proves the code actually being shipped. The local tree is installed EDITABLE: a non-editable install copies the whole checkout (node_modules included) into a PEP 517 build sandbox, which turned a 9-second install into one still unfinished after 20 minutes.
residuals.owner_rationale: Closed in this session; the walk passes in 47.6s standalone and inside a fully green 31/31 suite.

residuals.description: Nothing in the automated suite now asserts that the PUBLISHED `dabbler-ai-router` wheel is compatible with the shipping extension. That coverage did not lapse silently -- it moved from a pre-release test (where it was unanswerable) to a release-time check (where it is answerable), and it needs an owner there.
residuals.rationale: A pre-release test cannot know whether an unpublished version is on PyPI. The question belongs to the release walk, whose ordering this set's spec already mandates: publish `dabbler-ai-router` first, CONFIRM THE WHEEL IS LIVE, then publish the extension. Session 4 already owns the version floor and the post-install capability probe that make the check executable; what it should add is the post-publish half -- probe the registry wheel, not just the local one.
residuals.owner_rationale: Session 4 is the release gate and already declares the version floor and the capability probe. Asserting the floor against the PUBLISHED wheel is one step further along the same path, and it is the step that protects every existing project taking the Marketplace update.

residuals.description: Layer 3 is worker-count sensitive on this hardware. At the local default of 4 workers, specs intermittently fail waiting for the first tree row (icon-render-mechanism, blocked-by-prereqs, cancellation-state-file, manifest-diagnostic, migration-drift, default-module-scaffold-tree). At 2 workers -- the count CI uses -- the same suite is 31/31 green in 6.1 minutes. Each failure also passes when its spec is run alone, and icon-render-mechanism was additionally confirmed green at HEAD.
residuals.rationale: Not a behavioural regression: every affected spec passes in isolation and the whole suite passes at 2 workers, so the signature is Electron startup contention (each worker launches a full VS Code) rather than product behaviour. The run of record was taken at 2 workers and is recorded as such. Recorded rather than silently re-run-until-green, because a suite whose result depends on the worker count is a real cost even when it is not a defect.
residuals.owner_rationale: Belongs with whoever next revisits Layer 3 runtime/parallelism; the Step 9 review should decide whether lowering the local default to match CI earns its own change.

checklist.attestation: Operator-attested 2026-08-13. Two transitions left a record without a matching post: the operator-stop for the verification-reduction decision, and the last-logged-step. The orchestrator did post the checklist immediately before the operator brief, but the post landed before the decision was journalled, so the gate -- which looks for a post after the decision is recorded -- reads the window as missed. A passed window cannot be re-entered by a later post, so the honest exit is this waiver rather than a silent retry.
